request.instructions: You are an orchestrator agent that may delegate to child agents. Use graph__propose_spawn to propose a child when decomposition genuinely reduces risk or effort. Set each child's priority and budget_share to reflect how much that subtask matters. Use graph__request_skip_context to let a child see an ancestor's findings directly. Use graph__send_message to pass a finding to a sibling that has not run yet. After delegating, synthesize the children's findings into one final answer. State your final answer explicitly on the last line, prefixed with 'Answer:'.

messages.content: Produce a rigorous technical brief on database storage and transaction internals. For EACH of the following areas you must discuss at least three specific named mechanisms in real depth: (1) write-ahead logging, (2) MVCC, (3) LSM trees, (4) B+tree maintenance, (5) two-phase commit, (6) logical clocks, (7) quorum systems, (8) crash recovery . Use precise standard terminology for every mechanism you name. Be exhaustive: a shallow mention of an area does not count as covering it.

tools.name: graph__propose_spawn
tools.description: Propose spawning a child agent. The external graph controller must approve it.

tools.name: graph__send_message
tools.description: Propose sending a direct message to another node. The external graph controller must approve it.

tools.name: graph__request_skip_context
tools.description: Propose skipping context from a source node. The external graph controller must approve it.

response.content: I'll decompose this into two subtasks (storage-engine internals and distributed-coordination internals) and propose child agents for each, while preparing the synthesis.

arguments.objective: Deep technical coverage of single-node storage/transaction internals: WAL, MVCC, LSM trees, B+tree maintenance, and crash recovery.
arguments.instructions: For each of: write-ahead logging, MVCC, LSM trees, B+tree maintenance, crash recovery — name and explain at least three specific standard mechanisms (e.g., ARIES physiological logging, pageLSN/force-log-at-commit, group commit, InnoDB doublewrite, PostgreSQL xmin/xmax + VACUUM, InnoDB undo/read views, SSI, leveled vs size-tiered compaction, Bloom filters, memtable/SSTable flush, Lehman-Yao B-link trees, latch crabbing, suffix truncation, ARIES analysis/redo/undo with CLRs, fuzzy checkpoints, shadow paging). Use precise terminology and explain invariants and failure cases.

arguments.objective: Deep technical coverage of distributed transaction/coordination internals: two-phase commit, logical clocks, quorum systems.
arguments.instructions: For each of: two-phase commit, logical clocks, quorum systems — name and explain at least three specific standard mechanisms (e.g., presumed abort/presumed commit, 3PC, Paxos Commit, XA; Lamport clocks, vector clocks, Hybrid Logical Clocks, TrueTime commit-wait; majority quorums R+W>N, sloppy quorums with hinted handoff, flexible quorums/FPaxos, read repair). Explain safety/liveness properties, blocking behavior, and intersection invariants with precise terminology.
